text.p: Ronald Spinney, chief executive of UK property group Hammerson Plc, said on Monday he was encouraged the company had maintained the momentum of increasing net rental income for the first half of the year.
"We are the maintaining the momentum," he told Reuters in an interview after Hammerson had announced its results for the first half of 1996.
The group said net rental income for the period was 63.3 million stg, compared with 62.9 million stg for the first six months of 1995.

Spinney said he was "cautiously optimistic" that the UK property market would improve over the next nine months. This would benefit Hammerson, which was selective in its choice of properties and now had a well-balanced portfolio.
"Our prime focus has been on portfolio and asset management. We have started to step-up our development programme, which will improve shareholder value," Spinney said.

A 2.8 million stg reduction in income from Hammerson's 99 Bishopsgate property was because it had negotiated the surrender of a number of relatively short leases from tenants who had moved out after the property was severely damaged bomb-damaged.
These had been re-leased at current rents and now last well beyond the year 2000, Spinney said.
He said 5,300 square metres had alread been leased and he was confident leases on another 15,200 square metres would soon be agreed.
Spinney said the rebalancing of Hammerson's portfolio over the past three years meant it could now meet demands of both tenants and investors.
He said 54 percent of Hammerson's portfolio was in the UK, just over 17 percent in France, 17.5 percent in Germany, 1.0 percent in Spain and the balance in Canada.
Retail properties accounted for 58 percent of the total 1.9 billion stg portfolio, he added. "The core income is from our shopping centres," he said.
Spinney said property was already an attractive investment compared to gilts and equities, and this should continue over the next nine months.
